In an effort to rebuild parts of a social networking app, idempotency keys and database transactions were introduced to prevent duplicate processing, using Go for the hot path and Redis for short-lived caching, after a growing number of internal services needed a shared, reliable data contract. This effort reduced production incidents by 20%. Work also extended into an adjacent area of the stack: nightly batch jobs began overlapping and locking shared tables. The response there involved database indexes were reworked and a queue was introduced to serialize writes, built on Express.js with MongoDB for flexible document storage, and it reduced production incidents by 28%. Documentation was kept up to date so other people could pick up the work without much back-and-forth. Regular retrospectives helped surface which parts of the process needed the most attention. The lessons from this project shaped how subsequent releases were planned.
